comparator.name: Earth System Sciences (formerly Soil, Water, Atmosphere)
comparator.academicYear: Current 2026–2027 curriculum and published cohort-2025 course scheme, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme is the renamed successor to Soil, Water, Atmosphere and totals 180 EC. The 2026–2027 handbook specifies 117 EC of compulsory credited courses, a 3-EC mathematics or statistics choice, 18 EC of restricted advanced options, a 12-EC thesis and 30 EC of free electives. The comparison selects Mathematics Applied: Introduction and the first three 6-EC restricted options in official order—Hydrogeology, Programming in Python and Sedimentary Geology—because no named route or broader substantive preference distinguishes the options. Required non-credit safety modules and the personal-development pathway are acknowledged here but are not encoded as credit-bearing components.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme covers Earth systems, climate, soils, water, quantitative evidence and environmental research. Climate/atmosphere/geospatial data and soil/water/ecosystem resilience form two further independently evidenced, coherent and pairwise-distinct directions. All three are mechanically feasible; production stops at the maximum.

notes.text: WUR provides a prescribed specialist sequence in physics, chemistry, soil science, hydrology, meteorology, field measurement and advanced Earth-system options. UCR can combine substantial Earth science, climate, soils, water, ecology, observation and quantitative analysis, but it does not offer the same depth in atmospheric physics, meteorology, hydrology or field-based geoscience.
